stem: A 35-year-old man with HIV has taken zidovudine plus a protease inhibitor for many years. His viral load had been undetectable but is now climbing. Viral genotyping finds resistance mutations in the coding regions for the enzymes that these drugs target.
oneliner: 35M + HIV on zidovudine + protease inhibitor for years + viral load rising after suppression + resistance mutations in drug-target enzymes → which gene?
ask: Which viral gene most likely carries these mutations?

whyNot.A: **gag** codes for the structural capsid and matrix proteins (p24, p17), not drug-target enzymes
whyNot.B: **env** codes for the surface glycoproteins gp120 and gp41; its drug targets are entry inhibitors, not zidovudine or protease inhibitors
whyNot.C: **tat** is a regulatory transactivator of transcription, not an enzyme these drugs act on
whyNot.E: **nef** is an accessory protein that downregulates CD4 and MHC I; it is not a target of these drugs

why: Zidovudine blocks **reverse transcriptase** and protease inhibitors block **viral protease**; both enzymes (plus integrase) are encoded by **pol**. Years of therapy with incomplete suppression select **resistance mutations in pol**.
chain: Long-term therapy with missed doses or low drug levels
Mutants in reverse transcriptase and protease survive
Both enzymes are cut from the Gag-Pol polyprotein, coded by pol
Resistant virus outgrows the rest, viral load rises

idea.rule: HIV drug resistance maps to the gene of the enzyme the drug hits: pol for RT, protease and integrase.
also: Integrase inhibitor resistance is also in pol
Enfuvirtide (fusion inhibitor) resistance maps to env (gp41)
Gag-Pol is one polyprotein cleaved by viral protease
Maraviroc blocks host CCR5, not a viral enzyme

stem: Researchers extract the RNA genome from a newly isolated virus. A ribonuclease that cuts only single-stranded RNA destroys it. When added to cultured cells, the purified RNA produces no progeny virus; infection succeeds only if the virion's own polymerase is added. The virion has RNA-dependent RNA polymerase activity but no reverse transcriptase activity.
oneliner: Experiment: RNA genome cut by single-strand-specific RNase + purified RNA not infectious alone + infectious with virion polymerase + RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, no reverse transcriptase → genome type?
ask: Which genome type does this virus most likely have?

whyNot.B: Positive-sense RNA acts as mRNA, so the **purified genome alone would be infectious**
whyNot.C: A retrovirus carries **reverse transcriptase**, which this virion lacks
whyNot.D: The extracted genome is **RNA**, not DNA
whyNot.E: A double-stranded genome would **resist a single-strand-specific ribonuclease**

why: A negative-sense genome **cannot be translated directly**, so the virion must bring its own **RNA-dependent RNA polymerase** to make mRNA. Naked RNA is therefore **not infectious** without it.
chain: Virion packages its RNA-dependent RNA polymerase
Viral proteins are made and replication starts

idea.rule: The enzyme a virion must carry reveals its genome: negative-sense RNA brings RdRp; positive-sense RNA is infectious on its own.
also: Influenza, measles, rabies, Ebola and RSV are negative-sense and bring RdRp
Poliovirus and hepatitis A RNA is infectious when purified
Reovirus (double-stranded RNA) also packages its polymerase

stem: A 28-year-old man had a small painless sore on his penis that healed by itself within days. Three weeks later he has tender, matted nodes in the groin, some draining pus, with a groove running across the swollen nodes.
oneliner: 28M + painless genital ulcer that healed + weeks later tender suppurative inguinal nodes + groove sign → which organism and serovar group?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.A: Chlamydia trachomatis, serovars A to C
options.B: Chlamydia trachomatis, serovars D to K
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis, serovars L1 to L3

whyNot.A: Serovars A to C cause **trachoma** of the eye, not genital disease
whyNot.B: Serovars D to K cause **urethritis and cervicitis**, and stay in mucosal cells without invading nodes
whyNot.D: Chancroid gives a **painful** ulcer, not a painless transient one
whyNot.E: Donovanosis gives a **painless, beefy, slowly progressive ulcer**, not one that heals in days followed by suppurative nodes

answer: Chlamydia trachomatis, serovars L1 to L3
why: **Serovars L1 to L3** are the invasive types that travel through lymphatics, causing **lymphogranuloma venereum**. A brief painless papule is followed by **tender inguinal buboes** and the groove sign.
chain: Invasive serovars enter through a minor lesion
Organism spreads along lymphatics to inguinal nodes
Nodes become matted, tender and suppurative
The inguinal (Poupart's) ligament splits the nodal mass: groove sign

idea.rule: Chlamydia trachomatis serovar group predicts the site: A to C eye, D to K genital mucosa, L1 to L3 lymph nodes.
also: Serovars A to C: trachoma, a leading cause of preventable blindness
Serovars D to K: urethritis, cervicitis, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia
Serovars L1 to L3 infect macrophages and spread along lymphatics
Serovar L2: proctocolitis in men who have sex with men
